title: Flock Inbound Network Audit

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Flock Inbound Network Audit
communications.communication:
PUBLIC RECORDS REQUEST
California Public Records Act (Gov. Code §7920 et seq.) — Supplemental Request: Inbound Network Audit
Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (CPRA), Government Code §7920 et seq., I request access to and copies of a single, discrete category of public records maintained by the Tracy Police Department(“Tracy PD") in connection with its Flock Safety automated license plate reader (ALPR) system: the Flock “Network Audit” report reflecting inbound searches of Tracy PD's Flock network conducted by other agencies.
This request is intentionally narrow. It seeks one export object. It does not seek Tracy PD's own outbound search logs, investigative files exempt under Gov. Code §7923.600, or vehicle- or individual-identifying data.
RECORD REQUESTED
The Flock Safety “Network Audit” export, available within the Flock admin dashboard “Insights” tab, which Flock defines as searches of the organization's Flock network by any agency in the Flock system. For the avoidance of doubt, this request seeks the inbound record — that is, all queries run by any external agency or organization against Tracy PD's Flock cameras, network, or data.
The export should cover the period from the date Tracy PD first deployed, activated, or gained access to any Flock Safety camera or the Flock Safety platform (system inception), through the date this request is processed, and to the extent captured by the system should include, for each inbound query:
date and time of the search;
the searching agency or organization;
the user ID or operator identifier of the individual conducting the search;
the search parameters or terms; and
the stated reason or justification field associated with the search.
FORMAT OF PRODUCTION
Please provide the record in its original electronic, machine-readable format (CSV or spreadsheet). Per Flock Safety's Guide to Flock Safety Data for Open Records Laws (Sept. 3, 2025), these audit logs are accessible through the agency's Flock admin dashboard on the “Insights” tab, may be downloaded from the user interface as spreadsheets in 31-day increments, and Flock customer support is available to assist with downloads spanning larger timeframes. Accordingly, production of this record should impose minimal processing burden.
CERTIFICATION OF ABSENCE, IF APPLICABLE
If Tracy PD maintains that no responsive records exist for the requested period, or for any portion of it, please so state in writing, identifying the specific period for which no responsive Network Audit records exist.
WITHHELD RECORDS AND REDACTIONS
If any responsive record or portion thereof is withheld, please provide a written index identifying each withheld record or redaction, the specific exemption claimed, and the factual basis for the exemption, as required by Gov. Code §7923.010.
STATUTORY REQUIREMENTS
Under Gov. Code §7922.525, Tracy PD must respond within ten (10) calendar days of receipt, either providing the record, notifying me of the need for a 14-day extension, or stating the grounds for withholding. Failure to respond within the statutory period may constitute a waiver of applicable exemptions. If clarification is needed to identify the responsive record, please contact me promptly rather than treating any ambiguity as grounds for denial.
FEE WAIVER REQUEST
I request a waiver of any duplication or processing fees. Disclosure of this record serves the public interest by promoting transparency and accountability in law enforcement use of surveillance technology, and the record is not sought for commercial purposes. The requested records will be made available to the general public.
Thank you for your prompt attention to this request. Please direct any questions or correspondence to the contact information listed above.
Respectfully submitted,
___________________________________
Bill Baum
11/21/2026

Supplemental request — This request is limited to the single, discrete Flock “Network Audit” export reflecting inbound searches of Tracy PD's Flock network by external agencies. It is scoped to be independently answerable: any response, whether production or a written certification of absence, is fully responsive on its own terms.

title: Elaine Taylor Personnel Records & Brady/Giglio Disclosures  Oklahoma County District Attorney’s Office  Open Records Denial & Appeal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

REQUEST FOR REVIEW BY THE PUBLIC ACCESS COUNSELOR
51 O.S. § 24A.40(B) and (D)
Requester: Jennifer Holtzclaw. Public body: Oklahoma County District Attorney's Office. Original request submitted December 15, 2025 (MuckRock No. 199925).
Part 1. Entries for the Attorney General's form
Form field	Entry
Name	Jennifer Holtzclaw
Business or other affiliation	[None, or as Jennifer prefers]
Phone number	[__]
E-mail address	199925-35053988@requests.muckrock.com; jenniferholtzclaw@gmail.com
Mailing address	MuckRock News, DEPT MR 199925, 263 Huntington Ave., Boston, MA 02115 [or personal address]
City / State / Zip / County	[__]
Name of public body or public official	Oklahoma County District Attorney's Office (District Attorney Vicki Zemp Behenna). Responses signed by Assistant District Attorney Lisa Erickson Endres.
Date of records request	12 / 15 / 2025
How did you send your request?	E-Mail (through MuckRock to OCDA@oklahomacounty.org)
Have you received a response?	Yes
Did you request the records for a commercial purpose?	No
Have you consulted with an attorney about this request?	Yes
Has a lawsuit been filed related to this request?	No
Certification and signature	Signed and dated by Jennifer Holtzclaw
Part 2. Statement of the complaint
A. Summary
The Office left my request unanswered for 277 days because, by its own account, it "was filed away and not forwarded at the time." It then denied the request without a search, on grounds it has since abandoned or contradicted. On October 29 and 30, 2026, it denied my amended request in full and said it would not produce anything without a court order. On November 3, 2026, it reported an email search that returned no results, although its own correspondence in this matter, sitting in an Assistant District Attorney's mailbox, contains every term it purportedly searched. 
I ask the Counselor to find that the Office's delay was not prompt or reasonable, that its search was not adequate, that its withholding was a blanket policy rather than a decision about identified records, and that no search fee may be charged.
B. Timeliness
Section 24A.40(B) allows a request for review "not later than thirty (30) calendar days after the date of the denial." The Office treated my October 2, 2026, letter as an "Amended Request for Records" and denied it by standard form dated October 29, 2026, and letter dated October 30, 2026. This request is filed within 30 calendar days of that denial. The Office's November 3 search report followed the denial and is included as part of the Office's response. The delay claim is brought under § 24A.40(D), which permits review when a request "has not been returned promptly or reasonably" and states no filing period. 
C. History of the request
Date	Event	Ex.
Dec. 15, 2025	Request submitted through MuckRock to OCDA@oklahomacounty.org for records in the Office's possession, custody, or control concerning former OCPD forensic analyst Elaine Taylor, including Brady and Giglio determinations, notifications to prosecutors about her credibility or reliability, and communications with defense counsel and courts about her work.	A
Dec. 30, 2025, to Sept. 17, 2026	Eighteen follow-ups through MuckRock: Dec. 30, 2025, and Jan. 14, Jan. 29, Feb. 13, Mar. 2, Mar. 17, Apr. 1, Apr. 16, May 1, May 18, June 2, June 17, July 2, July 17, Aug. 3, Aug. 18, Sept. 2, and Sept. 17, 2026. No acknowledgment or response.	B
Sept. 17, 2026, 11:34 a.m.	Office staff member Brook Arbeitman forwards the request to ADA Endres: "This was filed away and not forwarded at the time. I scrolled to the bottom of the email and Jennifer Holtzclaw is involved."	C
Sept. 18, 2026	Denial. Grounds: (1) Ms. Taylor was never an Office employee and the Office has no personnel records, (2) files are not kept by investigator name and the Office "is not capable of performing the name search," (3) no time frame, (4) records available in court files, (5) an "original source" exemption cited as "51 O.S. §24A.A," and (6) § 24A.12.	C
Oct. 1 and 2, 2026	My letter asking the Office to withdraw the denial, supplying the case numbers, priority categories, and suggested search terms, and asking for record-by-record exemptions.	D
Oct. 26 and 27, 2026	My follow-up. ADA Endres replies that a response will come "on or before November 2, 2026."	E
Oct. 29 and 30, 2026	Standard form and letter. The Office treats the Oct. 2 letter as an amended request, states it located "electronic case file materials" containing information on Ms. Taylor and personnel records received from the City, withholds emails "regarding or discussing this witness" and a Brady/Giglio list under § 24A.12, and will produce nothing "without a valid court order." Exhibits 1 to 8 attached.	F
Nov. 3, 2026	Email search report: IT searched email "sent to or received from any Assistant District Attorney" from Jan. 1, 2014, to the present for ten terms. "The search did not return any matching results." The search took 3.5 hours.	G
Nov. 17, 2026	My letter to ADA Endres on the search report. It identifies messages the search should have returned, asks eight questions about how the search was run, and asks the Office to rerun it and produce or specifically withhold the results by December 2, 2026.	H

D. Issues for review
1. The 277-day delay was not prompt or reasonable. A public body "must provide prompt, reasonable access to its records," and any delay is limited to the time needed to prepare the records and to avoid excessive disruption of essential functions. 51 O.S. § 24A.5(6). The Office's own exhibit attributes the delay to the request being "filed away and not forwarded." No records were prepared during that time. The Attorney General has advised that a district attorney "has no authority to withhold public records from inspection and copying" and that prompt, reasonable access "generally may include only the time required to locate and compile such public records." 1999 OK AG 58, ¶ 15(2). In Branstetter v. Fallin, No. CV-2014-2372, Journal Entry of Judgment at 3-4 (Okla. Cnty. Dist. Ct. May 15, 2018), the court held that delays of about 11, 17, and 24 months, and "the process which resulted in the delays," were not prompt or reasonable, even though neither request had been formally denied. The Legislature's "emphatic message" is that "the public must have prompt and reasonable access to records" unless they are specifically excluded. Okla. Ass'n of Broadcasters, Inc. v. City of Norman, 2016 OK 119, ¶ 15, 390 P.3d 689.
2. The Office's search was not adequate. The November 3 report describes a search of every Assistant District Attorney's email from January 1, 2014, to the present, for ten terms. It returned zero results. Yet, the following messages fall within that description and contain listed terms:
•	My October 2, 2026, letter, sent by email to ADA Endres, acknowledged by her on October 27, and attached by the Office as its Exhibit 1. It contains all ten listed terms in the form searched, including "State v. Holtzclaw, Oklahoma County No. CF-2014-5869" and the suggested terms "Elaine Taylor," "E. Taylor," "Taylor," "lab," "DNA," "Brady," "Giglio," and "crime lab."
•	Ms. Arbeitman's September 17 and October 27, 2026, emails to ADA Endres (the Office's Exhibits ORR 1 and 2), with the subject line "... Concerning OCPD Forensic Analyst Elaine Taylor Crime Lab Records."
•	District Attorney David Prater's May 8, 2017, email to the "DA's Office - Assistant DA" distribution list, with copies to himself and to First Assistant District Attorney Scott Rowland, subject "OCPD Elaine Taylor": "ADAs: Please notify me immediately if you have a pending case wherein Elaine Taylor, OCPD DNA Lab employee, is endorsed as a witness." On May 9, 2017, ADA Sara Daly Robinett replied from DASARDAL@oklahomacounty.org: "CF-16-157, Scott Daugherty (burg 2) is pending with Elaine Taylor endorsed." Mr. Prater asked her for the OCPD case number "for them to track a lab number," and she supplied it. Mr. Prater then forwarded the thread to OCPD Chief Johnny Kuhlman with the note "Johnny, One more." The thread contains "Elaine Taylor," "Taylor," "DNA," and "lab." The City released it on July 28, 2017, in response to an open records request by a journalist, from the OCPD side of the thread (Bates C04298 to C04300, Ex. I). Every Assistant District Attorney on the distribution list received the first message.
Other City records show correspondence between Ms. Taylor, OCPD, and the Office that a competent search would have turned up.
•	Four entries in the "Suggested Contacts" folder of Ms. Taylor's OCPD mailbox, produced by the City: "Lori McConnell," dated July 9, 2014, "Daniel Gridley," dated October 3, 2014, "Rowland, Scott <sroland@oklahomacounty.org>," and "Salmon, John <john.salmon@oklahomacounty.org>" (Bates C00007, C00028, C00073, C00088, Ex. J). The Rowland and Salmon entries carry Outlook's no-date value, "1 Jan 4501." A version of Microsoft Outlook added an entry to this folder when the mailbox user sent email to an address not already in her contacts. The entries show that Ms. Taylor emailed two oklahomacounty.org addresses and emailed Mr. Gridley and Ms. McConnell in 2014. The production does not include those emails. The Office's copies would be in the accounts its search was meant to encompass.
•	An October 28, 2016, City notice placing Ms. Taylor on call for the jury trial week of October 31, 2016, in CF15001272 (Brown, "Murder 1"), with "Gridley" in the same entry, which she acknowledged the same day (Bates C02094, Ex. J). The notice is internal to the City. It shows that the Office had a pending murder prosecution with Ms. Taylor on call, and the Office's own communications with or about her in that case are within the request. A May 31, 2017, OCPD email in the same production lists a Taylor case for retesting under "burglary ADA Dan Gridley" (Bates C04298).
•	Four emails from OCPD Lt. Timothy Muzny to ADA Gayland Gieger at ggieger@oklahomacounty.org about this case, dated September 19, 2014 (OKC 2252, 2628) and September 25, 2014 (OKC 2577, 2631), from the City's production in Mr. Holtzclaw's federal civil case (Ex. K). Each names "Holtzclaw" in its subject line, and none uses the phrase "State v. Holtzclaw" or the case number. They show that a search for that exact phrase misses case email that refers only to "Holtzclaw." Two carry a Word attachment. The same production includes a July 24, 2014, email from Lt. Muzny to Capt. Ron Bacy (OKC 1136, duplicated at OKC 5692) reporting that while Mr. Gieger was reviewing cases with detectives "we called Elaine to get clarification about a saliva test," and that Mr. Gieger "would like us to be able to have their DNA tested before he takes the charges officially." That email was not sent to an Assistant District Attorney. Any Office record of that contact is within the request.
A search that misses the Office's own exhibits did not include the account of the Assistant District Attorney handling the request, did not include 2026, did not index message bodies or attachments, combined the terms so that all had to appear together, or omitted former employees' accounts. The report does not say who ran the search, on what system, with what query, or over which accounts. It also does not address the "electronic case file materials" the Office said on October 30 that it located, which are outside email.
3. The § 24A.12 withholding was a standing policy, not a decision about identified records. Section 24A.12 provides that a district attorney "may" keep litigation files and investigatory reports confidential. That language is discretionary. Mott v. Carlson, 1990 OK 10, ¶ 6 & n.4, 786 P.2d 1247, 1249 & n.4. 1999 OK AG 58, ¶ 8. A discretionary exemption requires a decision about the records at issue, and the decision is reviewable for abuse of discretion. Ross v. City of Owasso, 2017 OK CIV APP 4, ¶¶ 10-11, 18, 389 P.3d 396, 399-401. On October 30, the Office withheld emails "regarding or discussing this witness." On November 3, it reported that it found none. The withholding preceded any search. The Office's own exhibit states that it "elects to keep confidential from production its entire investigatory file as allowed by law." (Office's Ex. 5, "Commonly Claimed Exemptions.") A blanket decision made in advance for every request is not the case-by-case judgment Ross requires. Placing a record in a litigation or investigation file does not make it confidential. 51 O.S. § 24A.20. Moreover, Office-wide Brady and Giglio determinations about an analyst, and correspondence with OCPD about retesting her casework across many prosecutions, are not the investigatory file of any one single case.
4. The "original source" ground does not apply. The September 18 letter cited "51 O.S. §24A.A," which does not exist. The Office's exemptions page cites § 24A.20. The second sentence of § 24A.20 allows a law enforcement agency to deny access to a copy of a record in an investigative file only if the record "or a true and complete copy thereof is available for public inspection and copying at another public body." The Office's October 30 letter says the Taylor personnel records are sealed and disclosable only at the City's discretion, so they are not available for public inspection at OCPD. The Office's own emails, Brady and Giglio determinations, and correspondence did not originate with OCPD at all.
5. The Office's positions contradict each other. On September 18, the Office stated that it "does not have any personnel records" about Ms. Taylor. On October 30 it stated that it holds "personnel documents and records the DA has received from Oklahoma City for Elaine Taylor." On October 30, it withheld emails about Ms. Taylor. On November 3, it reported that none exist. On October 30, it said the September 18 letter gave "notification of possible search charges." The September 18 letter mentions none. The Office's March 13, 2020, filing in State v. Hayden, CF-2015-6800, which it attached as Exhibit 8, states that "the district attorney's office came into possession of certain personnel records of an endorsed witness" during the Holtzclaw post-trial litigation.
6. No search fee may be charged. No search fee may be charged "when the release of records is in the public interest," including release to taxpayers seeking to determine whether public officials are "honestly, faithfully, and competently performing their duties as public servants." 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4). The Office's procedures say the same (Office's Ex. 4, § II.G.3). Its fee schedule requires an estimate and prepayment of the minimum fee "prior to initiating the search" for any request it deems commercial or excessively disruptive (Office's Ex. 5). It gave no estimate and took no payment before the November 3 search. The schedule the Office attached bears a County Clerk file stamp of September 25, 2026.
E. What this request does not ask
The Court of Criminal Appeals has held that certain City personnel records filed in Holtzclaw v. Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

On November 13, 2026, EPA Region 7 issued an emergency RCRA permit authorizing the intentional detonation of 9,500 pounds of degraded lead near the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa. On November 19, Gov. Kim Reynolds’s spokesperson, Mason Mauro, told the Des Moines Register that the governor’s office only became aware of the planned detonation on November 16, when the Army issued a public advisory. A plume from the detonation could reach parts of Illinois.

I request all communications between the Illinois DPH, the federal EPA, and/or the Army between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

I also request all communications between DPH, the governor’s office, and/or any state agencies between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

I also request all communications between DPH and county and city authorities between November 13, 2026 and the date this request is processed regarding the planned detonation.

Please include the following records:

- All external correspondence, including emails, text messages, letters, memoranda, and attachments
- All records of meetings, including calendar invites, video and/or audio recordings, transcripts, meeting agendas, presentations, and follow-up materials

I request expedited processing on the grounds that there is an urgency to inform the public about the timeline of this planned explosion and communication between federal and state agencies. The records requested have far-reaching implications for public health. Delayed disclosure of these records would compromise the public’s timely understanding of critical government functioning. As a journalist actively reporting on public health and environmental management, disseminating information about it to the public through articles for WIRED—which publishes stories based on documents received under the FOIA outside its paywall as a matter of policy—I have a compelling need for expedited access to this information.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Molly Taft
